The baseline scenario in the PI has been identified as the continued use of non-renewable 
biomass in the absence of the project activity. A desktop30 and field31 baseline wood fuel 
use survey, as well as a fraction of non-renewable biomass survey32 was carried out in the 
PI area. The desktop baseline survey concluded that although the available literature 
sources are eligible for use (as stipulated by the CDM TOOL30), the sources are fairly old, 
published in 2012 and 2013 respectively, and may not accurately reflect the current 
conditions.  A field baseline survey was therefore recommended and carried out.

The sample size and selection were determined in accordance with the CDM guidance on 
“Sampling and surveys for CDM project activities and programmes of activities v04.0” with 
a 90/10 confidence/precision level. The number of households, population and average 
household size in the region was considered. The sample size of 271 was derived based 
on the total population of 1 211 015, with expected mean of 20, SD of 20, Z-multiplier 
1.645 and relative precision of 10 %. A sample of 300 households were selected on a 
simple random sampling basis across 20 villages in four regions within the K2C region. 
The Kitchen Performance Test protocol v4.033 of the Clean Cooking Alliance was followed 
and included a qualitative habit survey and daily wood use measurements over four 
consecutive days.

The sampling plan is intended to enable the discovery of unbiased and reliable estimates of

programmes of activities, version 4.

Parameter values may be estimated by sampling in accordance with Sampling Standard for a single

homogeneity of included PIs relative to the parameters of interest can be demonstrated or the 
differences among the included PIs is taken into account in the sample size calculation.

Fuel Efficient Cooking in South Africa by TASC is a voluntary Grouped Project (“GP”) aimed

specifically for this purpose. PI Implementers will be selected by TASC for their ability to 
handle the logistics of ICS distribution (storage, transportation, management etc.), but also 
for their ability to engage with local communities and identify suitable ICS recipients. 
Communities and individual recipients will be identified via an ongoing series of community 
sensitization meetings, which will introduce (amongst other things) the GP, the technology, 
and their impact.

The distribution of cookstoves is not mandated by South African law and the GP is a 
voluntary initiative.
